333745.title: Gunby's permeability formula conjecture for set-partition avoidance
333745.source_name: Ryan Alweiss, “Asymptotic results on Klazar set partition avoidance”, arXiv:1608.02279 (2018).
333745.literal_statement:
Let $\tau$ be a set partition of $[n]$. Its **permeability** $pm(\tau)$ is the minimum $k$ such that $[n]$ can be partitioned into $k+1$ intervals of consecutive integers, each containing at most one element from each block of $\tau$. Let $F_n(\tau)$ be the avoidance proportion defined in the paper. **Gunby's permeability conjecture.**

$$
F_n(\tau)=1-\frac{1}{pm(\tau)}.
$$

Gunby had proved the corresponding lower bound $A_n(\tau)\geq 1-1/pm(\tau)$ in general, and the source states that all the conjectures are true for $k\leq4$, but does not resolve the conjecture in general.
333745.assessment: Permeability formula is an asymptotic pattern-avoidance assertion with source-dependent F_n; finite proportions alone cannot refute its limiting exponent. No full-scope mechanism found.

333760.title: True minimum distance conjecture for the even-like LCD BCH code
333760.source_name: Shuxing Li, Chengju Li, Cunsheng Ding and Hao Liu, “Parameters of two classes of LCD BCH codes”, arXiv:1608.02670 (2017).
333760.literal_statement: Let $q$ be odd and $m \geq 2$. For an integer $t$ with $1 \leq t \leq \bar m$, let $\delta=(q^t-1)/2$ and let ${\mathcal{C}}_{(q,n,2\delta,\frac{n}{2}-\delta+1)}$ be the code from Theorem 1. **True minimum distance conjecture.** The code ${\mathcal{C}}_{(q,n,2\delta,\frac{n}{2}-\delta+1)}$ has true minimum distance $q^t-1$. Numerical experiments support this for $(q,m) \in \{(3,2),(3,3),(3,4),(3,5),(5,2),(7,2)\}$ and $1 \leq t \leq \bar m$; the theorem gives the lower bound $d \geq q^t-1$, while equality is conjectural in general.

333765.title: Cisinski's converse conjecture for the rational motivic spectrum
333765.source_name: Shane Kelly, “Some observations about motivic tensor triangulated geometry over a finite field”, arXiv:1608.02913 (2016).
333765.literal_statement:
Let $SH(\mathbb{F}_q)^c_\mathbb{Q}$ be the compact rational stable motivic homotopy category over $\mathbb{F}_q$, and let $\operatorname{Spc}$ denote its tensor-triangular spectrum. **Cisinski's conjecture.** If

$$
\operatorname{Spc}(SH(\mathbb{F}_q)^c_\mathbb{Q}) \cong \mathbb{Q},
$$

then the Beilinson–Parshin conjecture holds and rational equivalence agrees with numerical equivalence. This is presented as a converse to the implication that these motivic conjectures determine the tensor-triangular spectrum; the source does not establish the converse or indicate that it has been resolved.

333771.title: The higher-dimensional lower-bound conjecture for ordinary hyperplanes
333771.source_name: Simeon Ball and Joaquim Monserrat, “A generalisation of Sylvester's problem to higher dimensions”, arXiv:1608.03189 (2016).
333771.literal_statement:
For $d\geqslant4$, let $e_d(n)$ denote the minimum number of ordinary hyperplanes determined by a set of $n$ points in the relevant $d$-dimensional geometric setting. **Higher-dimensional lower-bound conjecture.** There is a constant $c_d$ such that, for $n$ sufficiently large,

$$
e_d(n)\geqslant \frac{1}{(d-1)!}n^{d-1}-c_dn^{d-2}.
$$

This extends the proposed lower-bound pattern from ordinary lines and planes to dimensions at least four. The statement is presented as a conjecture, and no resolution is supplied in the source.
333771.assessment: Asymptotic ordinary-hyperplane lower bound in every d≥4; degeneracy loopholes would require source hypotheses and yield no significant correction credit.

333775.title: The forbidden Berge hypergraph conjecture for the 4-cycle
333775.source_name: Richard Anstee and Santiago Salazar, “Forbidden Berge Hypergraphs”, arXiv:1608.03632 (2016).
333775.literal_statement:
Let $\mathrm{Bh}(m,F)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $m$-vertex Berge hypergraph containing no Berge copy of the hypergraph represented by the incidence matrix $F$. Let $\1_1$ be the one-row, one-column incidence matrix and let $C_4$ denote the incidence matrix of a 4-cycle; write $\1_1\times C_4$ for their product.

**Forbidden Berge hypergraph conjecture for the 4-cycle.**

$$
\mathrm{Bh}(m,\1_1\times C_4)=\Theta(m^2).
$$

This conjecture is used in the paper to establish a classification result for the case $k=5$. Its status is not specified in the supplied text.

333828.title: Fractional arboricity bounded-diameter conjecture
333828.source_name: Martin Merker and Luke Postle, “Bounded Diameter Arboricity”, arXiv:1608.05352 (2016).
333828.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $k\geq1$ be a natural number, and let $\varepsilon>0$ be real. Write $\Upsilon_f(G)$ for the fractional arboricity and $\Upsilon_d(G)$ for the minimum number of forests whose components all have diameter at most $d$.

**Fractional arboricity bounded-diameter conjecture.** There exists $d(k,\varepsilon)$ such that, if

$$
\Upsilon_f(G)\leq k-\varepsilon,
$$

then

$$
\Upsilon_{d(k,\varepsilon)}(G)\leq k.
$$

This is proposed as a strong bounded-diameter consequence of fractional arboricity being separated from the integer arboricity threshold. The paper presents it as an additional open conjecture.
333828.assessment: Uniform bounded-diameter forest decomposition for every k and positive gap. No concrete obstruction to all diameter choices identified.

333835.title: Consistency of LSA from the consistency of T and PFA
333835.source_name: Nam Trang, “PFA and guessing models”, arXiv:1608.05726 (2016).
333835.literal_statement:

$$
\operatorname{Con}(T)\Rightarrow\operatorname{Con}(\textsf{LSA})\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{Con}(\textsf{PFA})\Rightarrow\operatorname{Con}(\textsf{LSA}).
$$

The conjecture proposes that both $T$ and $\textsf{PFA}$ have at least the consistency strength of $\textsf{LSA}$, a strong determinacy theory whose consistency was recently established according to the source. The relative consistency implications remain conjectural.

333845.title: The circular altitude conjecture for the third Mycielskian of $K_6$
333845.source_name: John Bamberg, Brian Corr, Alice Devillers, Daniel Hawtin, Irene Pivotto and Eric Swartz, “The circular altitude of a graph”, arXiv:1608.06127 (2016).
333845.literal_statement:
Let $K_6$ be the complete graph on six vertices, and let $\mathcal M^3(K_6)$ denote its third Mycielskian. Write $\alpha^\circ(G)$ for the circular altitude of a graph $G$ and $\chi_c(G)$ for its circular chromatic number. The preceding bounds give

$$
8\leqslant \alpha^\circ(\mathcal M^3(K_6))\leqslant \chi_c(\mathcal M^3(K_6))\leqslant 9.
$$

**Circular altitude conjecture.**

$$
\alpha^\circ(\mathcal M^3(K_6))=9
$$

and hence

$$
\chi_c(\mathcal M^3(K_6))=9.
$$

The circular chromatic number of $\mathcal M^3(K_6)$ is a prominent open problem in circular colouring. The conjecture is based on trial computer computations and would determine both the circular altitude and circular chromatic number in this case.
333845.assessment: 55-vertex third Mycielskian exact circular-order obstruction needs exhaustive all-order certificate; coloring an instance or using bounds 8..9 is insufficient.

333855.title: The modified conjecture for cohomology classes of fixed forest shape
333855.source_name: Hannah Alpert, “Restricting cohomology classes to disk and segment configuration spaces”, arXiv:1608.06612 (2016).
333855.literal_statement:
Let $\operatorname{Conf}_n$ be the configuration space of $n$ disks, and let $H^{\underline{m}}(\operatorname{Conf}_n)$ be the subspace of cohomology generated by ordered forests whose nontrivial connected components have sizes given by the finite multiset $\underline{m}$. Write $r_{\min}(n,\underline{m})$ for the infimal $r$ such that restriction is not injective on this subspace, and $r_{\max}(n,\underline{m})$ for the supremal $r$ such that restriction is not zero there. **Modified conjecture.** There exists a constant $C>1$ such that, for all $n$ and all finite multisets $\underline{m}$ of integers greater than $2$,

$$
\frac{r_{\max}(n,\underline{m})}{r_{\min}(n,\underline{m})}\leq C.
$$

This modification compares only classes with the same list of connected-component sizes, avoiding the counterexample supplied by comparing matchings with paths. The source presents it as an attempted replacement for the false naive conjecture; no resolution is supplied here.
333855.assessment: Requires geometric cohomological restriction ratios for all forest shapes; previously refuted naive matching/path comparison explicitly excluded. No new family obtained.

333932.title: Erdős's conjecture on the first unresolved triangle count
333932.source_name: Alyssa Epstein, Adam Lott, Steven J. Miller and Eyvindur A. Palsson, “Optimal point sets determining few distinct triangles”, arXiv:1609.00206 (2017).

Let $F(t)$ denote the maximum number of points that can be placed in the plane while determining exactly $t$ distinct triangles.

**Erdős's conjecture.** Any set of seven points in the plane determines at least four distinct triangles; consequently,

F(3)=6.

333946.title: The star conjecture for minimum Rényi entropy of connected graphs
relevant_proof_bodies_read: selected prior quadratic-moment proof context, not full paper
333946.source_name: Michael Dairyko, Leslie Hogben, Jephian C. -H. Lin, Joshua Lockhart, David Roberson, Simone Severini and Michael Young, “Note on von Neumann and Rényi entropies of a Graph”, arXiv:1609.00420 (2016).
333946.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with at least one edge, let $L(G)=D(G)-A(G)$ be its combinatorial Laplacian, and define the scaled Laplacian by $\rho(G):=L(G)/\operatorname{tr}L(G)$. For $\alpha>1$, the Rényi $\alpha$-entropy of $G$ is

$$
H_\alpha(G)=\frac{1}{1-\alpha}\log_2\left(\sum_i\lambda_i^\alpha\right),
$$

where the $\lambda_i$ are the eigenvalues of $\rho(G)$. **The star conjecture.** For $\alpha>1$ and any connected graph $G$ on $n$ vertices,

$$
H_\alpha(K_{1,n-1})\leq H_\alpha(G).
$$

This is the Rényi-entropy analogue of the conjecture that the star minimizes von Neumann entropy among connected graphs. The paper establishes the corresponding unrestricted extremal bounds but leaves the connected-graph minimum as a conjecture.
333946.assessment: Primary Conjecture3.3 read; alpha=2 already proved. Spectral majorization shortcut fails even on P4. Full all-alpha target unresolved here.

g(n)=\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\quad\text{if }n\ne(2k+1)^2-3\quad\text{for some }k\in\mathbb{N}.

333968.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a tree on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $Delta\leq n-1$. The **almost-dendrimer conjecture.** If $G$ has maximal Graovac-Ghorbani index among all such trees, then $G$ is an almost dendrimer $T_{n,Delta}$. The conjecture proposes the maximizer among trees with prescribed maximum degree; the source gives no resolution.

333977.title: Distinct-degree strengthening for graphs with small homogeneous sets
333977.source_name: Bhargav Narayanan and István Tomon, “Induced subgraphs with many distinct degrees”, arXiv:1609.01677 (2017).
333977.literal_statement:

$$
\hom(G)<\frac{n}{k-1},
$$

then

$$
f(G)\ge k.
$$

This is presented as a strengthening of the paper's main theorem and is left as a suspected statement rather than proved.

334022.title: The Vojta conjecture for integral points on hyperelliptic curves
334022.source_name: Nicole R. Looper, “Dynamical Galois groups of trinomials and Odoni's conjecture”, arXiv:1609.03398 (2016).
334022.literal_statement:
For each integer $d\ge 3$, let $f\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ have degree $d$ and nonzero discriminant, and let $h(f)$ be the maximum of the logarithmic heights of the coefficients of $f$. **Vojta's conjecture.** There exist constants $C_1=C_1(d)$ and $C_2=C_2(d)$ such that, whenever $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$ satisfy

$$
y^2=f(x),
$$

then

$$
h(x)\le C_1(d)\cdot h(f)+C_2(d).
$$

This uniform height bound is invoked in the paper to control the indices at which the arboreal Galois extensions can fail to be maximal. The source treats it as an assumed conjectural input, so its status here is open.

334037.title: Alon and Tarsi's shortest circuit cover conjecture
334037.source_name: Yezhou Wu and Dong Ye, “Circuit Covers of Cubic Signed Graphs”, arXiv:1609.03620 (2016).
334037.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a 2-edge-connected cubic graph. A **shortest circuit cover** of $G$ is a circuit cover having minimum total length, denoted by $\operatorname{scc}(G)$. **Alon and Tarsi's conjecture.** Every 2-edge-connected cubic graph has a shortest circuit cover with length at most

$$
\frac{7|E(G)|}{5}.
$$

The conjecture improves the general $5|E(G)|/3$ bound for 2-edge-connected graphs and would give a sharp universal bound for cubic graphs. It is also known as the Shortest Circuit Cover Conjecture and, as noted in the source, implies the Circuit Double Cover Conjecture.

334155.title: The ordered Erdős–Hajnal tower-growth conjecture for tight paths
334155.source_name: Dhruv Mubayi, “Variants of the Erdos-Szekeres and Erdos-Hajnal Ramsey problems”, arXiv:1609.07670 (2016).
334155.literal_statement:

$$
\operatorname{twr}_{t-2}(n^c)<r_k(k+1,t;P_n)<\operatorname{twr}_{t-2}(n^{c'}).
$$

334155.assessment: Tower-scale asymptotic Ramsey assertion; finite colorings cannot resolve full growth. No uniform stepping-up route developed.

334218.title: Planar triangulations have total domatic number at least two
relevant_proof_bodies_read: successor Observations5–20/Lemma18 proof chain; only two-color result, not full proof of three-color target
334218.source_name: Wayne Goddard and Michael A. Henning, “Thoroughly Distributed Colorings”, arXiv:1609.09684 (2016).
334218.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a planar triangulation of order at least $4$. A **total dominating set** is a vertex set whose every vertex has a neighbor in the set, and the **total domatic number** $\tdom(G)$ is the maximum number of pairwise disjoint total dominating sets in $G$.

**Planar triangulation conjecture.** Every planar triangulation $G$ of order at least $4$ satisfies

$$
tdom(G) \ge 2.

334228.title: The diameter conjecture for lattice polytopes
334228.source_name: Antoine Deza and Lionel Pournin, “Improved bounds on the diameter of lattice polytopes”, arXiv:1610.00341 (2016).
334228.literal_statement:
Let $\delta(d,k)$ denote the maximum possible diameter of a lattice $(d,k)$-polytope, where $d$ is the dimension and $k$ is the maximum number of lattice points on any edge. A Minkowski sum of lattice vectors means the Minkowski sum of the corresponding line segments or lattice-vector generators, considered up to translation. **Diameter conjecture.** $\delta(d,k)$ is at most

$$
\left\lfloor\frac{(k+1)d}{2}\right\rfloor,
$$

and this bound is achieved, up to translation, by a Minkowski sum of lattice vectors. The conjecture would identify the general upper bound with the lower bound supplied by primitive lattice polytopes; the cited work establishes the lower bound for $k\leq 2d-1$, while the matching upper bound and the asserted extremal form remain unresolved in the supplied text.

334290.title: Quasi-line graph 5/6 conjecture
334290.source_name: Daniel W. Cranston and Landon Rabern, “Short fans and the 5/6 bound for line graphs”, arXiv:1610.03924 (2016).

334302.title: Operator-theoretic generalization of Denis–Schanuel's conjecture
334302.source_name: F Pellarin, “On a variant of Schanuel conjecture for the Carlitz exponential”, arXiv:1610.04048 (2017).
334302.literal_statement:
Let $q=p^e$ with $e>0$, let $s\geq0$, let $K_s=\mathbb{F}_p(\theta,t_1,\ldots,t_s)$, and let $L_s$ be the smallest $\mu$-difference subfield of $\mathbb{K}_s$ containing $K_s$ and every element regularly $\mu$-algebraic over $K_s$. For $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in\mathbb{K}_s$, write $g_i=\exp_C(f_i)$. If the $f_i$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{F}_q(t_1,\ldots,t_s)[\theta]$, then $n$ of the $2n$ elements

$$
f_1,\ldots,f_n,g_1,\ldots,g_n
$$

are regularly $\mu$-independent over $L_s$.

**Operator-theoretic generalization of Denis–Schanuel's conjecture.** The asserted regular $\mu$-independence holds.

The conjecture refines the earlier transcendence-degree formulations by incorporating the difference operator $\mu$. The source gives no proof or resolution.

334309.title: The polylogarithmic susceptibility conjecture for bounded-degree graphs
334309.source_name: Itai Benjamini, Luiz Renato Fontes, Jonathan Hermon and Fabio Prates Machado, “On an epidemic model on finite graphs”, arXiv:1610.04301 (2025).

334313.title: Minimum-degree criterion for zero-forcing graphs
334313.source_name: Daniel Weißauer, “A zero-sum problem on graphs”, arXiv:1610.04407 (2016).
334313.literal_statement:

$$
\delta(G) \geq D(\mathcal G)-1,
$$

then $G$ is zero-forcing for $mathcal G$. The paper notes that the corresponding chromatic-number condition yields a subgraph of this minimum degree, but that existing results do not force a sufficiently large complete minor; whether this condition suffices remains open.

334538.title: Lin's extremal-preimage conjecture for the Jacobian on the Hardy space
334538.source_name: Sauli Lindberg, “On the Hardy space theory of compensated compactness quantities”, arXiv:1611.02223 (2016).
334538.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{H}^1(\mathbb C)$ be the Hardy space, let $J$ denote the Jacobian, and let $\dot{W}^{1,2}(\mathbb C,\mathbb C)$ be the homogeneous Sobolev space. For $u$ in this space, write $u_{\bar z}$ for its antiholomorphic derivative and let $\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal H^1_S}$ be the indicated Hardy-space norm.

**Lin's conjecture.** For every $h\in\mathcal{H}^1(\mathbb C)$, there exists $u\in\dot{W}^{1,2}(\mathbb C,\mathbb C)$ such that

$$
Ju=h
$$

and

$$
\|Ju\|_{\mathcal H^1_S}=\int_{\mathbb C}|u_{\bar z}|^2.
$$

The conjecture strengthens surjectivity of the Jacobian by requiring a solution attaining the stated norm identity for every Hardy-space datum. The source reports substantial partial results, including a closed set of data containing all extreme points of the unit ball, but leaves the full assertion open.
334538.assessment: Norm-attaining Jacobian preimage for every Hardy datum is stronger than surjectivity; no exact functional counterexample or full Lean bridge found.
